searchedFor: grep for CI_DEFINING_PATHS / definesCi consumers repo-wide
finding.summary: Gate 1b's CI_DEFINING_PATHS omits files ci.yml executes from the merge ref — `Dockerfile.playwright` is the whole browser lane, and a branch may edit it and still auto-promote
finding.evidence: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:528` runs `docker build -t wafflebase-playwright -f Dockerfile.playwright .` and `:533` runs that image as the entire `verify-browser (22.x)` lane. Both come from the PR MERGE REF, exactly like `ci.yml` itself. `Dockerfile.playwright` is not matched by any entry in `CI_DEFINING_PATHS` (scripts/agent/checks.mjs:123-135), so `definesCi("Dockerfile.playwright")` is false and `ranBaseCiDefinition` (scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:222) returns true. A branch whose Dockerfile CMD is `true` produces a genuinely green CI run at the genuine path, gate 1 passes, gate 1b passes, and mark-ready posts the hand-off comment that now asserts "the CI definition that run executed came from `main`" (scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:382-388). The same holds for `packages/cli/vitest.config.ts` and `packages/design-sandbox/vitest.config.ts`, which choose which tests vitest collects for those lanes. The fix belongs on the new code: add these paths to CI_DEFINING_PATHS (and, since checks.test.mjs asserts the mirror is a superset of `harness.config.json`'s `ci.ciConfig`, the extra entries are already permitted there). Note the doc's admitted residue is "a branch can weaken its own tests"; a Dockerfile that defines the lane's entrypoint is not test content, so this is inside the claim the gate makes, not the residue it disclaims.

verdict.reason: Verified directly. CI_DEFINING_PATHS (scripts/agent/checks.mjs:123-135) contains 11 anchored globs, none of which can match `Dockerfile.playwright` (the builder at checks.mjs:140-153 anchors both ends and `*` does not cross `/`), so `definesCi("Dockerfile.playwright")` is false and gate 1b (mark-ready.mjs:205-226, 236-282) records no hit. Yet .github/workflows/ci.yml:528 builds that Dockerfile and :530-537 runs the resulting image as the ENTIRE verify-browser lane, both from the PR merge ref; Dockerfile.playwright:7 (`CMD ["node", "./scripts/verify-browser-lanes.mjs"]`) is where the lane's entrypoint is chosen, so editing that line guts the lane while the covered `scripts/verify-*.mjs` entry is untouched. packages/cli/vitest.config.ts and packages/design-sandbox/vitest.config.ts also exist and are unmatched (`packages/*/package.json` does not cover them). I searched for a counterexample guard and found none: harness.config.json:52-62's ci.ciConfig lists no Dockerfile or vitest config (no JSON file in the repo contains the string "Dockerfile"), the only other Dockerfile.playwright handling is lane SELECTION not promotion refusal (scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs:205-208), and the promote job (.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1453-1508) adds no path check — it gates on ci conclusion + panel blocked, then runs mark-ready, whose gates are enumerated at mark-ready.mjs:310-315. mark-ready.mjs:29-32 states the agent App is blocked only from .github/workflows/**, so a top-level Dockerfile push is reachable, and the hand-off comment (mark-ready.mjs:394-399) then asserts the CI definition came from main. The disclaimed residue at checks.mjs:116-121 covers "a branch weakens its own tests"; a container entrypoint is lane definition, not test content. Blast-radius lane: a guard with a reachable bypass; major.
